svg.title: What lies under the ground
svg.desc: A section through the rotor wall and the vacuum gap drawn to scale, with radius increasing down the page. At the top, the city: a megaframe pier, a low building standing on sockets, a tree, a person and a shallow lake. Under the ground lie a 2 m ground deck with lawn trays and lake tanks, a 7 m utility deck with mains, the tree’s root vessel and a person on a walkway, a 10 m transit deck with a freight vehicle and a reservoir, and an 11 m root deck where the pier flares into its root, with crush members and a catch layer over the liner. Below the liner at 2,530 m are 0.70 m of carbon tension bands, then insulation and radiator panels. Below the skin a vacuum gap of 20 m, which the wall’s heat crosses as infrared light, separates the rotor from the stationary shell: a cooled absorber face over a catcher layer, then shell structure drawn only in part. Radii 2,500, 2,502, 2,509, 2,519, 2,530 and 2,552 m are marked, with a 10 m scale bar.
svg.text: A section through the rotor wall and the gap below it, all to scale. The city at the top, the stationary shell at the bottom.
carry the pull of the air
